set.hook: Christophe Quéant's starred market kitchen on Place Carnot, three-course lunch at 50 €.
set.why: The house is old and the façade modern; inside, MICHELIN describes a beige room of exposed stone a short walk from the Hôtel-Dieu. Christophe Quéant came through the Robuchon and Ducasse kitchens and cooks seasonal plates on classical foundations. Gault&Millau's 2026 review tasted foie gras with langoustines and artichoke, lobster salad with tarragon and romesco, and a verbena soufflé with grapefruit sorbet. In the evening the shortest of the three menus is called Petit Pasumot.
set.verdict: The MICHELIN page still shows one star after the 2026 selection, and Gault&Millau 2026 gives 13/20, calling the cooking bourgeois and regional, technically sure. Lunch at 50 € is the sensible way in; dinner climbs to 178 €. Diners' reviews note tables set close together and some noise, and one called the sole and the soufflé the high points of an otherwise uneven six courses.

set.caveat: Closed Sunday and Monday, no Tuesday lunch; book, the room is small and the tables close

Gault&Millau's 2026 entry puts the bill at 95 to 190 € a head before wine.

This is the more formal of Beaune's two starred rooms and the one that runs lunch at the weekend, which makes it the safer Sunday booking during the auction. Expect hotel-restaurant polish rather than surprise, and prices to match.

set.hook: Mikihiko Sawahata grills beef and eel over binchotan at a ten-seat counter on rue Maufoux.
set.why: About ten stools face the grill, so the meal is watched as much as eaten. Mikihiko Sawahata's speciality is sumibi-yaki over Japanese binchotan: Miyazaki wagyu, or Limousin beef aged 40 days, or fish. Gault&Millau's 2026 entry adds sushi, tempura, eel and beef tongue off the charcoal. Sachiko, his wife and co-owner, runs a sake and wine list that Jancis Robinson found long on lesser-known Burgundy at fair prices, and young growers eat here.
set.verdict: Gault&Millau selected it for 2026 at 45 to 63 € a head before drinks, well under the starred tables, and the crowd of local winemakers says more than any guide. Reviews disagree on the food: some find the produce and tempura exact, others call portions thin. Go for the grill and the bottles, sit at the counter, and book: ten seats fill.

set.hook: The Escoffier family's 1996 bistro off Place Carnot, now a sharing-plate wine room under the son.
set.why: Pierre and Fabienne Escoffier opened Ma Cuisine in 1996 in a former bookshop down the passage Sainte-Hélène, and it became the table where the wine trade ate oeufs en meurette and pigeon with bottles from a deep cellar. Their son Mathieu, who also took the name to Singapore in 2018, now runs it. Gault&Millau's 2026 review describes a looser room built for sharing: prawns, pata negra, Galician beef, a regional cellar, very little by the glass.
set.verdict: Treat it as a call-first address this year. Gault&Millau's 2026 review (12/20) describes a working dinner room, but MICHELIN's page carries an undated 'temporarily closed' notice, and the February 2026 reopening in our old record was not found. If it is open, go for the cellar and a late booking; do not promise guests the old canon menu.

set.hook: Wine bar and bistro on pedestrian rue Monge: oeufs en meurette, bourguignon, 600 bottles.
set.why: A small bistro and wine bar on a pedestrian street off Place Monge, with a terrace outside and Mickael Thibert in the kitchen. The plates are the ones Burgundy is known for: eggs poached in red wine with lardons, beef braised for hours, and a fish of the day. The list is the surprise for the size of the room: more than 600 references by Gault&Millau's count, more than 500 by the tourist office's.
set.verdict: Gault&Millau keeps it in its 2026 selection at about 45 € a head before wine, which is honest money for the canon cooked properly. Reviewers say it fills fast and to come early if you have not booked. It is the straight answer to a guest who wants bourguignon in Beaune without the tourist-menu version.

set.hook: Romain Escoffier's Bib Gourmand on Boulevard Foch, the menu rewritten every fortnight.
set.why: The carte and the set menu drawn from it change every two weeks, and MICHELIN singles out the lamb from the Ferme de Clavisy as the kind of local produce Romain Escoffier builds on. Diners come back for the lamb confit and the desserts, and for a sommelier working a cellar MICHELIN puts at about 800 references. Gault&Millau rates it 12/20, a Table Gourmande, at 27 to 37 € a head before wine.
set.verdict: The best-value serious cooking on the boulevard, and the Bib on its MICHELIN page and in the 2026 tourist office listing backs that. Reviews also report a cool welcome and a strict booking policy, including a 66 € charge for cancelling inside twelve hours. Book ahead for Fridays and weekends, and confirm the penalty when you do.

summit.title: Two stars and a grill
summit.story: Beaune's serious dinners sit within a few hundred metres of each other, inside the ramparts or on the boulevard that rings them. Le Carmin, on Place Carnot, is Christophe Quéant's house: trained with Robuchon and Ducasse, he sells a 50 € three-course lunch under a MICHELIN star. Clos du Cèdre, starred since 2022, cooks matured Charolais beef in a wine merchant's manor on Boulevard Maréchal-Foch, and is the only one of the three to serve lunch at the weekend. On rue Maufoux, Mikihiko Sawahata grills Limousin beef aged 40 days over binchotan at a counter of about ten seats, while Sachiko, his wife, pours sake and lesser-known Burgundy to the growers who eat there.
summit.where: Le Carmin, Place Carnot; Clos du Cèdre, Boulevard Foch; Bissoh, Rue Maufoux

bouchons.title: The canon, three ways
bouchons.story: Burgundian cooking is wine cooking: eggs poached in red, beef braised in it for an afternoon. Le Bistrot Bourguignon, on pedestrian rue Monge, serves oeufs en meurette and bourguignon from Mickael Thibert's kitchen with a list of more than 600 references. Ma Cuisine, opened by Pierre and Fabienne Escoffier in 1996 down the passage Sainte-Hélène, is now run by their son Mathieu as a sharing-plate wine room, though MICHELIN shows it temporarily closed. On Boulevard Maréchal-Foch, La Table du Square holds a Bib Gourmand for a menu rewritten every fortnight around lamb from the Ferme de Clavisy, at 27 to 37 € a head by Gault&Millau's count.
bouchons.where: Le Bistrot Bourguignon, Place Monge; Ma Cuisine, Place Carnot; La Table du Square, Boulevard Foch
